output.murderer: Dr Casimir Vauthier, the family physician
output.reasoning:
The blow happened when the repeater sounded, and the repeater's own strike is the anchor. Félix's watch is 20 minutes slow (8:40 at the nine o'clock bell), so his "thump, then ten hours and some quarters" at 10:18 by his watch is 10:38 true. Girard's watch is 4 minutes slow: the hall clock is 12 minutes fast (Lina's regulator comparison at the hall's ten), and Girard's hall-face reading of 11:02 when he came in fixes his offset at -4. His "faint quick bells" at 10:34 by his watch are therefore 10:38 true. Two independent witnesses confirm the repeater struck at 10:38, which is the blow time.

Working the rest of the timeline with these offsets: the kitchen clock is about 25 minutes fast, not the 15 Rosa believes. That makes Lina's arrival in the kitchen at 10:22, within the five-minute rule, and it makes the piano (heard in the kitchen 10:58 to 11:11) run from 10:33 to 10:46 true. Girard's piano reading (10:29 by his watch) gives the same start, 10:33. Odile was at the piano from 10:33 to 10:46 and is cleared, since the piano was audible in the kitchen throughout the blow time. Lina and Rosa corroborate each other in the kitchen from 10:22 onward, and Girard was in the street. That leaves Félix and Casimir.

Casimir says he left the piquet at 10:45 by his watch, which with his own stated +2 offset is 10:43 true. The piano, the kitchen clock and Girard all put his departure at 10:33. His account of the cigar case being in his coat in the hall is contradicted by Odile, who says he had run out of cigars. That is a lie that moves his departure 10 minutes later and puts him in the salon at the blow time. Félix heard someone go quickly up past the library at 10:35 true, the thump and repeater at 10:38, and someone come quickly down at 10:41. Casimir's route fits all of these: salon at 10:33, up to the atelier by 10:36, the blow at 10:38, down at 10:41, and back in the salon by 10:46 when the piano stopped. The regulator reads 10:05, although Lina saw it running at 10:20. Someone set its hands back and stopped it after she left, and the only person in the atelier then was the murderer. Setting it to 10:05 would place the crime during the piquet, when Casimir was with Odile, so it serves Casimir's alibi. Félix remains a weaker alternative, since his account of the stairs fits Casimir better and Casimir's timing is the one that contradicts four independent sources.
